card.content:
## Key Recession Metrics

### Longest Recession
**Great Depression: 10 years** (1929-1939)

The longest economic downturn in U.S. history.

### Highest Unemployment
**25% during Great Depression**

Peak unemployment rate reached in 1933.

### Most Severe GDP Drop
**-30% (1929-1933)**

Largest GDP contraction in U.S. history.

markdown.title: U.S. Recessions: Historical Overview
markdown.content:
# U.S. Recessions: Historical Overview

## Key Findings

1. **Great Depression (1929-1939)**: Longest and most severe economic downturn
   - Duration: 10 years
   - GDP decline: 30%
   - Peak unemployment: 25%

2. **Great Recession (2007-2009)**: Longest since World War II
   - Duration: 18 months
   - GDP decline: 4.3%
   - Peak unemployment: 10%

## Trends

- Recessions have become shorter over time (post-WWII trend)
- Financial crises cause deeper contractions than non-financial recessions
- Policy interventions have helped reduce severity in recent decades
